So I brewed an APA yesterday (recipe below) and had several issues. I’ve been all grain brewing for a while now and these problems just go to show that it doesn’t matter how ‘efficient’ you think you are, you’re always prone to getting it wrong!!

  1. Online supplier pre-crushed the malt when I specified uncrushed – technically not my mistake, but I had to deal with a slightly over crushed grain bed, which made issue 2 much worse;

  2. My mash tun grain screen malfunctioned – I’ve been using an adapted SS hose braid as a grain screen and it got stuck! I still had 1/3 of wort to drain and had to sterilise my gloves and get my hands into the mash (sigh). Turns out the braid contracted and wasn’t letting anything through. Terrible image for you but essentially I ‘milked’ the braid to get things flowing…Eventually I got it all out but it is pretty cloudy. I’ve placed an order for a bazooka screen this morning!! Time to upgrade.

  3. Had a boil over – simple mistake and all my fault. I got distracted by the dog and had the burner turned right up. Luckily I caught it just has it happened and only a little went over the top. Left me with a very messy burner and pot though.

After the boil over it all went smoothly and I ended up with 23 litres super hopped beer. Fingers crossed fermentation goes well!

APA – Recipe (25L)

OG: 1.060 FG: 1.010

Malt

  • Pale Ale Malt – 5kg

  • Light Crystal Malt – 100g

  • Munich Malt – 1kg

  • Wheat – 250G

Hops schedule

  • Colombus – 11g (60 mins)

  • Citra – 11g (60 mins)

  • Mosaic – 11g (60 mins)

  • Citra – 6g (15 mins)

  • Mosaic – 11g (15 mins)

  • Irish Moss – 1 Tsp (10 mins)

  • Citra – 6 g (5 mins)

  • Mosaic – 11g (5 mins)

  • Citra – 11g (flameout)

  • Mosaic – 20g (flameout)

Dry hop – Mosaic 20g (day 7)

Yeast - Fermentis Saf US-05 (US-56) - ferment - 14 days

had to sterilise my gloves and get my hands into the mash

Was it really necessary to sterilize? You're going to boil for 60min, if bacteria can grow after that then you've got another problem.

When I brew I always have a bucket of sanitizing solution handy. When I gloved up it was a quick exercise to first stick them in the sanitizer then into the mash. I agree, the boil would likely kill off anything nasty, but my view is if you have the ability to sanitize you should (within reason)

I worry about how much sanitize I use though. Even though it is food safe, it is a chemical that goes through heating and could change the flavor (even slightly). It would all depend on how much you use though. Back when I bottled I always wondered if it changed things.

It is an interesting thought and could be a good experiment: The same recipe and ingredients, one brewed using sanitized equipment, one brewed with no sanitizer (just being extra careful of bugs), then compare the flavours

It might be tough using no sanitizer but maybe someone who bottles their beer can try half the bottles only cleaned with boiling water and the other half using one-touch sanitizer or something like that. I would be curious to hear if there was a difference. Same with not using sanitizer on the mashing or anything pre-boil and cleaning the carboy with just boiling water.
